newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares climb, led up by Ericsson.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares climb, led up by Ericsson.

text.p: Sweden's stockmarket posted good gains on Monday which surprised market players with telecoms giant Ericsson leading the rise.
The Stockholm general index climbed 0.49 percent to 2160.19 after shares worth 3.1 billion crowns were traded.
Brokers said the rise was unexpected with fears that the drugs sector would be hit by nerves in the U.S. ahead of the election next month.
But the drugs sector index rose 0.26 percent with Astra edging up 0.5 to 310 crowns and Pharmacia & Upjohn up one at 250.5 crowns.

Ericsson was the star performer of the day, closing 4.5 crowns higher at 189 crowns. Brokers attributed this to gains on Wall Street on Friday and ahead of its nine month result on Tuesday which was forecast to show a 29 percent rise.
"The bourse ended stronger than everyone had expected in the morning," a broker said. "Ericsson was very strong during the day and Astra held up better than expected."
Car safety equipment maker Autoliv posted a 14 percent rise in nine month profits, much in line with market expectations, and closed three higher at 286.5 crowns.
